notices.description: The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.
notices.plain: Youth and Community Development awarded Grand Street Settlement Inc a $514,103 contract through a negotiated acquisition, without open competition, for the Healthy Families program in a low-income neighborhood.

notices.short_title: Technical Assistance Services for Literacy Support
notices.description: DYCD's capacity-building and technical assistance programs support DYCDs contracted providers in the areas of Organization Development, Fiscal Management, Strength-Based Approaches to Service Delivery, Career Development, Developing a Safe and Supportive Environment, Adult Literacy Support, Mental Health Support and Case Management to enhance program services. These services have been determined to be of high need to support our contracted providers and the work they do for the City of New York.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development renewed a $1,711,779 contract with Literacy Assistance Center to provide technical assistance to its contracted providers on topics including fiscal management, career development and adult literacy support.

notices.short_title: COMPASS Programs in Public Schools - Elementary
notices.vendor_name: New York Junior Tennis League Inc.
notices.description:
COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.
08X152 P.S. 152 Evergreen, 22K197 P.S. 197 - The Kings Highway Academy, 21K215 P.S. 215 Morris H. Weiss,19K325 The Fresh Creek School, 29Q037 Cynthia Jenkins School, 27Q042 P.S./M.S 042 R. Vernam
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded New York Junior Tennis League Inc. a $102,265,200 contract to run COMPASS after-school, summer and holiday programs at several elementary schools, chosen from competing proposals within a pre-qualified list.

The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Southern Queens Park Association Inc. $1,504,962 for the COMPASS Center-Based Middle program in Queens 12, chosen from competing proposals limited to pre-approved vendors.
